full_judgment:
10. PW 1 Kasem Ali Bepari is the complainant of the case who stated in his evidence that he took settlement of the case land measuring 96 decimals as khas land of the Government 5 years ago and since them he has been owning and possessing of the same. He further stated that the case land has subsequently been mutated is his name following which he is paying rent to the Government. He further stated that he grew Gobara Paddy in 50 decimals of the case land by the western side of the plot and grew Nyatpasha paddy in the remaining 46 decimals by the eastern side of the plot and the crops grew well, He went on to state that on 7th Agrahayan, 1399 BS i.e. the date of the occurrence, the accused persons illegally trespassed into the case land and cut and took away Gabara paddy from 50 decimals of land causing him a loss of Taka 5500.00. He also stated that the accused persons also damaged half ripe Nyatpasha paddy from 46 decimals of the case land causing him a less of Taka 3000.00. 

 20. From the evidence discussed above, it is clearly found that the witnesses examined in the case are natural and probable witnesses. Moreover, PWs 2-5 are found to be totally independent and disinterested. All the PWs uniformly and consistently proved that the complainant on taking settlement of the case land from the Government as khas land 5 years ago duly obtained possession therein and since then he has been owning and possessing the same. It has been proved by convincing and corroborative evidence that on the date of the occurrence the accused persons illegally trespassed into the case land and defying the protest of the complainant dishonestly cut and took away Gabra paddy from 50 decimals of case land and thereby caused him a wrongful Joss of Taka 5,500.00. It has also been proved by overwhelming evidence that the accused persons also caused damage to the complainants Nyatpasha paddy in 46 decimals of the case land causing him a loss of Taka 3000.00. The fact of growing of the case crops by complainant Kasem Ali Bepari and dishonestly cutting and taking away of the same and damaging the half ripe Nyatpasha paddy by the accused have been proved by most cogent and reliable evidence. The defence has miserably failed to shaken the corroborative testimony of the prosecution witnesses in any material particular. Since the growing of the case crops by the complainant has been proved beyond reasonable doubts and the act of theft and damages of the same by the accused' have been proved to the hilt, the learned Courts below were perfectly justified in convicting and sentencing the accused persons under sections 379/427 of the Penal Code.
